name: Hjerpefinte (centre, NTHF)
source_text: Center starts with the puck out on the blade to the right of the slot, and shoots directly into the right corner. Only works against a goalie expecting a Hjerpe

approved_reading.text: Yes, but the trick is that you can do a hjerpe from the same position. So you are dependent on the goalie predicting a hjerpe and opening up the right corner
approved_reading.applies_to: the reading (set-up, ccw push into the right corner, goalie opening the right corner); the trace stays proposed

reading: DESIGNED by Claude; reading approved by the user on 2026-10-10 (approved_reading) and revised on 2026-10-12 (user_revision). The centre stands in its slot about one puck diameter in front of the E blue line, back to the goal, the puck resting against the blade on the right (-y): the Hjerpe stance, from which the puck can also be carried round to the left. The goalie covers the right side. Reading a Hjerpe, it slides to the left post just as the centre turns counter-clockwise with a short step and pushes the puck from rest (a push, not a strike: CLAUDE.md 'Slide or bounce') straight into the right corner it has just opened.

start.why: at rest against the blade, on the goal side, where the Näcka shot meets it (trace.nacka.v1 contact.shot local point [2.58, 26.82])

keys: one puck diameter in front of the E blue line (user, 2026-10-12): puck near edge about 25 mm ahead of the line
moves: step of 20 mm up the slot with the shot (a longer, faster push than v1: the shot is 48 mm longer)

turns: counter-clockwise turn: the blade pushes the puck from rest toward the right corner

keys: covers the right side (y = -12 mm): the straight shot is closed
moves: bites on the Hjerpe threat: slides to the left post (y = +28 mm) as the centre shoots, opening the right corner

events.why: the centre starts the counter-clockwise turn
the goalie reads a Hjerpe and starts to slide to the left post

limitations: No recording: the whole move is DESIGNED from the one-line NTHF text and the user's description (2026-10-10, 2026-10-12).

The blue line position (x = 95 mm) comes from the preview overhead mapping (data/geometry.json image_to_world, ASSUMED scale); 'one puck distance in front' is read as the puck's near edge about one diameter ahead of the line.
The goalie's covering position (y = -12 mm), the timing of its slide (0.22-0.34 s, starting 30 ms before the turn) and its end position (y = +28 mm) are ASSUMED.
The centre's fake is the stance only (no separate fake movement): the goalie reacts to the Hjerpe threat.
Contact rules, ice friction and figure geometry as every move-engine trace (scripts/shotlib): restitution 0.5 assumed, friction from the spjass fit, AI-modelled molds at the preview scale.
tuning: v2 (2026-10-12), scripts/build-move.py --quick scans: from 48 mm further back the v1 push (181 -> 205 deg in 70 ms, 14 mm step) scores but reaches the net too slowly to stay robust under +25% ice friction; 181 -> 205 deg in 60 ms with a 20 mm step gives 692 mm/s, the right corner at y = -17.6 mm, a push of 39 small touches (peak 44 mm/s) and 11/11 robustness variants.

user_revision.text: The hjerpefinte only works when the goalie expects a hjerpe. Now it leaves the room open the entire time which does not make sense in real life. I want the video to emphasise that you need to make the opponent think you do a hjerpe and then shoot it straight. The goalie should cover the side and then open it as the center shoots. Also it must start a bit further back, maybe one puck distance in front of the blue line
user_revision.applied: v2: the centre starts at arc 184 mm (puck centre x = 136 mm, about one puck diameter in front of the E blue line at x = 95 mm, preview scale); the goalie covers the right side (y = -12 mm) and slides to the left post (y = +28 mm) from 0.22 s, just before the shot at 0.25 s; turn 60 ms and step 20 mm so the longer shot keeps its speed.
